summary: Improvement remains strategically coherent and the codified priority order is still correct. Priority 1 remains the strongest portfolio bottleneck, but it is materially stronger than earlier in the week because the Phase 1 canonical TDE-first substrate is now selected, validated, and aligned across the Improvement operating model, plan, interfaces, decisions, and TDE entry surface. Priority 3 also advanced materially on 2026-03-21: the broader minimum improvement interface rollout seed is now published and explicit product-side deployment steps have been completed in Security, Task Management, Governance, and Interfaces. Priority 2 remains the clearest unchanged gap: pinned-lane delivery into PXS with version truth, rollback semantics, and verification still has no new execution evidence.
materialChanges: TOP_PRIORITIES.md was reviewed against the full Improvement product stack and current TDE execution reality; no stale or incorrect priority wording was detected, so the canonical priority surface remains unchanged.

The product moved from post-substrate ambiguity into early operational rollout: the minimum improvement interface rollout seed is now explicit in `products/improvement/04-execution/MINIMUM_IMPROVEMENT_INTERFACE_ROLLOUT_SEED_2026-03-21.md`.

Priority 3 now has four explicit product-side deployment steps completed in Security, Task Management, Governance, and Interfaces, strengthening the evidence base for cross-product rollout rather than leaving the interface as a product-local intention only.
Priority 2 still shows no new delivery evidence; interim-copy distribution drift remains the main unchanged execution exposure.

topPriorities.title: Converge improvement execution into one canonical TDE-first system of record
topPriorities.why: Improvement still needs one explicit, reusable, evidence-backed execution path; otherwise signals can fragment across non-canonical surfaces and weaken traceability.
topPriorities.currentStatus: The low-risk Phase 1 substrate is selected in D-003 and is now supported by PLAN, OPERATING_MODEL, INTERFACES, TDE entry-surface alignment, and exemplar validation around OPS-2026-066 through OPS-2026-069. The main remaining gap is broader operational adoption rather than substrate ambiguity.
topPriorities.nextStep: Use the now-aligned Phase 1 substrate as the bounded base for further minimum product-side improvement interface rollout across remaining active products.

topPriorities.title: Ship A-005 into PXS through a pinned lane with version truth, rollback, and verification semantics
topPriorities.why: Improvement delivery still depends on interim-copy behavior, so downstream drift risk remains active and installed-state truth is weak.
topPriorities.currentStatus: No new progress is visible in the reviewed product stack or execution evidence. Interim-copy lanes still appear to be the baseline mechanism, and the pinned-lane target is not yet the lived distribution path.
topPriorities.nextStep: Implement the pinned lane as an operational path with machine-checkable installed-version truth, explicit rollback behavior, and a verification pass that closes the interim-drift gap.

topPriorities.title: Roll out the minimum improvement interface across active products, starting with mandatory incident-to-improvement conversion
topPriorities.why: The proof case and intake contract exist, and deployment has started, but the broader product-side interface is still not deployed across the full active portfolio.
topPriorities.currentStatus: IMP-ERR-20260315 remains the completed end-to-end proof case. OPS-2026-066 through OPS-2026-069 remain the reference intake batch. The rollout seed is now explicit, and deployment evidence exists for Security, Task Management, Governance, and Interfaces. The interface is still not yet deployed across the remaining active products.
topPriorities.nextStep: Extend the same minimum product-side improvement interface into the next remaining active product surface after Interfaces, preserving the selected-priority -> rollout-intake -> product-surface evidence chain.

constraints: Improvement must remain evidence-backed and must not become a narrative-only reporting layer.
Improvement does not own canonical task or decision state; that boundary remains with Task Management / TDE.
No authority or security boundary changes should be made as part of improvement rollout without explicit escalation.
